children: rose on Wednesday after the Mexican broadcaster said it would buy AT&T's Mexican unit, in a move welcomed by investors that will set up a showdown with telecoms giant America Movil

The acquisition, if completed, would significantly expand Televisa’s telecom footprint, with Scotiabank analysts estimating its share of Mexico’s fixed and wireless subscribers would more than double to 19% from 8%.

The increase in scale would strengthen Televisa’s position in a market dominated by America Movil, controlled by the family of Mexican billionaire Carlos Slim. However, analysts cautioned that integrating the new business and competing in Mexico’s costly, fiercely contested telecom sector could limit the benefits of the deal.
Televisa could become a stronger rival, with more growth opportunities, by selling service bundles and earning more from its existing customers, analysts at UBS said.
"We believe the transaction could be positive for the Mexican telecom industry. Consolidation usually leads to a greater focus on profitability, returns and cash generation," analysts at UBS said.
The deal, worth $2 billion in cash and done in tandem with privately held Fintech Holdings, pushed shares up around 6% at 1944 GMT.
The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. Investors aren't likely to expect major gains until the combined company delivers on expected results.
The valuation represents a significant discount to comparable telecom companies in Latin America, but the acquisition carries some execution risks, Santander analysts wrote in a note.

"Value will be created through turning around AT&T Mexico’s operations which have historically struggled (low margins) and eventually build out a convergent fixed-mobile offering ... which could also prove challenging," the note said.
UBS also flagged execution as a challenge ahead for the new group.

AT&T Mexico still requires network modernization and investment, particularly in 5G, and the deal's success will depend on THE management's ability to improve the network while generating cash, the bank said.
Santander analysts expected little immediate effect on America Movil, citing its scale and dominant market position.
Scotiabank, however, said the deal could intensify competitive pressure because the relatively low purchase price could allow Televisa and Fintech to devote more capital to network investment.
Deal values AT&T Mexico at $2 billion in cash with Fintech Holdings
Combined company could hold 19% of Mexico fixed and wireless subscribers, Scotiabank estimates
